newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end with strong gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end with strong gains.

text.p: Feb 3 - U.S. interest rate futures closed with strong gains and in the upper portion of daily ranges. A January NAPM index that was below expectations added a boost to debt futures, sending March bonds above resistance near 111-18/32 and 112-03/32, which prompted technical buying. Traders expect no change in policy from the FOMC meeting that begins tomorrow. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))

Even though prices paid and employment sectors of the index showed increases, the market ignored these components, as June T-bonds broke above chart resistance at 111-28/32 and 112-03/32, which in turn prompted technical buying.
Collins said prices now are likely to remain steady or possibly ease back a bit -- to the 111-20/32 to 111-16/32 in March bonds -- ahead of the U.S. employment report for January due out on Friday.
Traders have already factored in no change to monetary policy coming from the meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee that begins Tuesday.
Non-farm payroll employment Friday is expected to show an increase of 237,000 jobs according to a Reuters poll of economists.

Collins said Smith Barney, however, is estimating payrolls at only about a 150,000-job increase, largely because January had almost five full workweeks in it this year, and hence post-Christmas layoffs were more likely to be carried over into January.
"If we do come in with a modest (jobs) number, it could take off," with March bonds rising to the 114-00 area, he said.

At settlement, March T-bond futures were up 21/32 point at 112-03/32, 10-year T-notes were 12/32 higher at 109-05/32 and muni-bonds were 19/32 higher at 115-27/32. June IMM T-bills were up 0.02 at 94.86 and Eurodollars were three points higher at 94.31. ((--Chicago Derivatives desk (312)408-8750)) ((E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
